title: The adjunction $j_!\dashv Lj^*$ on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$
statement:
For a commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$ and an open immersion $j\colon U\to X$ of the setting,
the adjunction

$$
j_!\dashv Lj^*\qquad\text{between }D_{\mathrm{cons}}(U,\Lambda)\text{ and }D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)
$$

of the restricted functors of [def-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek] and [def-sfb-dc-upper-star] is the
restriction along the fully faithful inclusions of the ambient adjunction
$D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$, transported along the identification $D(j^*)\cong Lj^*$.

proof.text: Work throughout with module objects over the same pulled-back commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$. The extension-by-zero clause of [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] specifies $j_!=j^{\mathrm{lin}}_!\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j}$, with underlying abelian sheaf $j^{\Ab}_!M$, and asserts that this functor is exact and left adjoint to the module pullback $j^*$. These are the underived functors used below, for every commutative condensed $\Lambda$; no assertion about a compactification lower shriek is needed. To establish exactness of $j^*$ with the same generality, use its definition [def-sfb-module-upper-star]: $j^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_j}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(j^*_{\Ab})$. The abelian-sheaf pullback $j^*_{\Ab}$ is additive and exact by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-exact], applied with coefficient category $\mathcal A=\Ab$, not with a category depending on $\Lambda$. By [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], the abelian-sheaf tensor is closed symmetric monoidal and preserves colimits in each variable. Preservation of the zero object and binary coproducts gives additivity of tensoring in each variable. Thus tensoring by each of $\Lambda_X$, $j^*\Lambda_X$, and $\Lambda_U$ is right exact, as required in [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-lifted]. The transport construction [def-sfb-modobj-transport] gives the equality $U_{j^*\Lambda_X}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(j^*_{\Ab})=j^*_{\Ab}\circ U_{\Lambda_X}$ of underlying-sheaf functors. Applying that lifted-exactness lemma with $F=j^*_{\Ab}$ and $G=\operatorname{mapMod}(j^*_{\Ab})$ proves that the transport factor is additive and exact. For the second factor, [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] states that $\alpha_j:j^*\Lambda_X\to\Lambda_U$ is an isomorphism for every condensed ring; [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] explicitly identifies it as an isomorphism of ring objects. Parts 4 and 5 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] therefore give $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_j}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_j^{-1}}$ and exactness of this restriction functor. Their hypotheses hold in $\Sh(U_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$: it is abelian with equalizers and coequalizers, its tensor is closed symmetric monoidal and colimit-preserving, and $j^*\Lambda_X$ is commutative because the ring isomorphism $\alpha_j$ identifies it with the commutative ring object $\Lambda_U$. Hence extension of scalars is exact as well. Composing these two exact factors proves exactness of the specified module pullback $j^*$, without an admissibility hypothesis on $\Lambda$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], the two exact functors send quasi-isomorphisms of complexes to quasi-isomorphisms and give termwise functors $D(j_!)$ and $D(j^*)$ on the unbounded derived categories. The exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] identifies the total left derived functor $L(j_!)$ with $D(j_!)$, the total right derived functor $R(j^*)$ with $D(j^*)$, and $Lj^*=L(j^*)$ with $D(j^*)$. All these total derived functors are everywhere defined. To check the meaning of this last assertion in [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors], the system for a quasi-isomorphism $s:K\to I$ has comparison $D(j^*)(s)^{-1}:D(j^*)I\to D(j^*)K$; for $t:P\to M$, the other system has comparison $D(j_!)(t)^{-1}:D(j_!)M\to D(j_!)P$. These maps are natural, are identities at $s=1_K$ or $t=1_M$, and are all isomorphisms. In [def-pc-essentially-constant-ind-diagram] take the distinguished index to be $1_K$, its section to be the identity, and the common index for $s:K\to I$ to be $s$ itself. The arrows of indices are $1_K\to s$, represented by $s$, and $1_s$; the required factorization is $1_{D(j^*)I}=D(j^*)(s)\circ D(j^*)(s)^{-1}$. In [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram] take the distinguished index to be $1_M$, its retraction to be the identity, and the common index for $t:P\to M$ to be $t$ itself. The arrows of indices are $t\to1_M$, represented by $t$, and $1_t$; the required factorization is $1_{D(j_!)P}=D(j_!)(t)^{-1}\circ D(j_!)(t)$. Thus these are also the everywhere-defined derived functors in the general derived-adjunction theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] (Stacks Tag 09T5) to $G=j_!$ and $F=j^*$, using the underived adjunction of step 1 and the everywhere-defined derived functors of step 2. This gives $L(j_!)\dashv R(j^*)$. Substitute the canonical exact-functor identifications of step 2 to obtain the ambient adjunction $D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$. These identifications are those in the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]; hence this is the adjunction induced from the specified underived adjunction, rather than a new choice of an unrelated right adjoint.

proof.text: Let $\theta:D(j^*)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lj^*$ be the inverse of the canonical exact-pullback identification from [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. If $\Phi_{K,L}:\operatorname{Hom}(D(j_!)K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(K,D(j^*)L)$ denotes step 3's ambient Hom-bijection, define $\widetilde\Phi_{K,L}(a)=\theta_L\circ\Phi_{K,L}(a)$. Its inverse sends $b:K\to Lj^*L$ to $\Phi_{K,L}^{-1}(\theta_L^{-1}\circ b)$. The two inverse identities follow by cancellation of $\theta_L$ and $\theta_L^{-1}$, and naturality is explicit: for $u:K\to K_1$, $v:L\to L_1$ and $a:D(j_!)K_1\to L$, one has $\widetilde\Phi_{K,L_1}(v\circ a\circ D(j_!)(u))=\theta_{L_1}\circ D(j^*)(v)\circ\Phi_{K_1,L}(a)\circ u=Lj^*(v)\circ\widetilde\Phi_{K_1,L}(a)\circ u$. This explicitly constructs $D(j_!)\dashv Lj^*$.

proof.text:
Write $\iota_U$ and $\iota_X$ for the inclusions of the bounded constructible categories. By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] these are full subcategories, with the same Hom-sets as the ambient derived categories. The definitions [def-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek] and [def-sfb-dc-upper-star] give the restricted functors and their comparison with the ambient functors after inclusion for the general coefficient ring $\Lambda$. In particular, the current extension-by-zero definition equips each object $D(j_!)(\iota_U K)$ with its bounded-constructibility property and gives the inclusion comparison with identity components. We use its inverse as the comparison $c$ below, so the direction agrees with the Hom formulas. For $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(U,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)$, define the required Hom-bijection by the composite
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)}(j_!K,L)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})}(D(j_!)\iota_UK,\iota_XL)
\xrightarrow{\ \widetilde\Phi\ }
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\Mod_{\Lambda_U})}(\iota_UK,Lj^*\iota_XL)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{D_{\mathrm{cons}}(U,\Lambda)}(K,Lj^*L).$$
Here the equalities use the inclusion comparisons, or equivalently the corresponding canonical Hom-bijections if restrictions commute up to isomorphism. More explicitly, put $F=D(j_!)$, $G=Lj^*$, $f=j_!$ and $g=Lj^*$ for the last two restricted functors. Write the natural inclusion comparisons as $c_K:F\iota_UK\xrightarrow{\sim}\iota_X(fK)$ and $d_L:G\iota_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}\iota_U(gL)$. The displayed map sends $a:fK\to L$ to the unique $b:K\to gL$ with $\iota_U(b)=d_L\circ\widetilde\Phi(\iota_X(a)\circ c_K)$. Its inverse sends $b$ to the unique $a$ with $\iota_X(a)=\widetilde\Phi^{-1}(d_L^{-1}\circ\iota_U(b))\circ c_K^{-1}$. Full faithfulness gives these unique morphisms, and cancellation of $c,c^{-1},d,d^{-1}$ and the two ambient inverse identities proves the two restricted inverse identities. For $u:K'\to K$ and $v:L\to L'$, write $\Psi$ for this restricted map. Naturality of $c$, step 4, and naturality of $d$ give, in order,
$$\iota_U\Psi(v\circ a\circ f(u))=d_{L'}\circ G(\iota_Xv)\circ\widetilde\Phi(\iota_Xa\circ c_K)\circ\iota_Uu=\iota_U(g(v))\circ d_L\circ\widetilde\Phi(\iota_Xa\circ c_K)\circ\iota_Uu=\iota_U(g(v)\circ\Psi(a)\circ u).$$
Faithfulness of $\iota_U$ proves naturality in both variables. This defines the adjunction in the statement. For the ambient unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$ of step 4, the restricted unit and counit are characterized by $\iota_U(\eta^{\mathrm{cons}}_K)=d_{fK}\circ G(c_K)\circ\eta_{\iota_UK}$ and $\iota_X(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{cons}}_L)=\varepsilon_{\iota_XL}\circ F(d_L^{-1})\circ c_{gL}^{-1}$. Thus these are precisely the ambient unit and counit restricted using the inclusion comparisons. For the left triangle, naturality of $c$ gives $\iota_X(f(\eta^{\mathrm{cons}}_K))=c_{gfK}\circ F(\iota_U\eta^{\mathrm{cons}}_K)\circ c_K^{-1}$. Substitute the unit and counit formulas and cancel $c_{gfK}^{-1}c_{gfK}$ and $d_{fK}^{-1}d_{fK}$; naturality of $\varepsilon$ then gives
$$\iota_X(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{cons}}_{fK}\circ f(\eta^{\mathrm{cons}}_K))=\varepsilon_{\iota_XfK}\circ FG(c_K)\circ F(\eta_{\iota_UK})\circ c_K^{-1}=c_K\circ\varepsilon_{F\iota_UK}\circ F(\eta_{\iota_UK})\circ c_K^{-1}=1.$$
For the right triangle, naturality of $d$ gives $\iota_U(g(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{cons}}_L))=d_L\circ G(\iota_X\varepsilon^{\mathrm{cons}}_L)\circ d_{fgL}^{-1}$. Substitution cancels $d_{fgL}^{-1}d_{fgL}$ and $G(c_{gL}^{-1}c_{gL})$, and naturality of $\eta$ gives
$$\iota_U(g(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{cons}}_L)\circ\eta^{\mathrm{cons}}_{gL})=d_L\circ G(\varepsilon_{\iota_XL})\circ GF(d_L^{-1})\circ\eta_{\iota_UgL}=d_L\circ G(\varepsilon_{\iota_XL})\circ\eta_{G\iota_XL}\circ d_L^{-1}=1.$$
The last equality in each calculation is the corresponding ambient triangle identity. Faithfulness of the inclusions proves both restricted triangle identities.
